_comment:
Hand-curated optimal_swell_dir (true-north degrees, the swell bearing the spot works best on) for spots whose ray-cast value is wrong. Applied by pipeline/enrich.py as Algorithm 2d, AFTER Algo 2 (raycast), Algo 2b (orientation-derived fallback) and Algo 2c (tier preserve-guard) — so it is the LAST writer of optimal_swell_dir in enrich and beats every other source, LLM verification included. Slug derivation mirrors pipeline/db_import._slugify (via enrich._slug_for) so re-enrich looks up by the same key that lands in the spots table. Stored alongside spot_orientations.json: the durable, re-enrich-survivable override mechanism for optimal_swell_dir, which had none.

WHY THIS FILE EXISTS. interpret.directional_gain targets optimal_swell_dir and falls back to orientation_deg only when the optimal is null — so a hand-corrected orientation never reaches the rating on a spot that has an optimal. All ten spots below already carried orientation_source="manual" and still rated off a swell arriving from behind the land. The cause is the ray-cast: _first_seaward_entry returns "open" when a ray exits the spot's own landmass and never returns, which is correct for a seaward ray leaving a beach and wrong for a landward ray leaving a finite island — a continent blocks because the ray never escapes within the 3000 km fetch, an island does not. Honolua Bay scored dir_gain 1.000 on an 84-degree east swell that would have to cross the whole of Maui. Prior research concluded that binary ray-casting structurally cannot model refraction and that the answer is nearshore model output (CDIP MOP / NWPS), so this is a durable human override, NOT a raycast fix.

KNOWN LIMIT — THE RAYCAST HALF IS NOT GUARDED. pipeline/sw1_raycast.py:353 (_apply_raycast_result) writes spot["swell_window_arcs"] and spot["optimal_swell_dir"] unconditionally; its `preserve` flag gates only swell_window_source. sw1_raycast runs as its own workflow (.github/workflows/sw1-raycast.yml, mode=full) and writes spots_enriched.json WITHOUT going through enrich, so a full raycast run will still overwrite every value in this file. That guard was deliberately left out of round one: it cannot be verified until the next full raycast, which is rare. MITIGATION: after any `sw1-raycast mode=full`, re-run enrich so Algo 2d re-applies these values, and check the review-branch diff before merging it.

FRAME CAVEAT, TRUE OF EVERY VALUE BELOW. Each source describes the DEEP-WATER swell direction. optimal_swell_dir is compared against the model's direction at a nearshore node 1-4 km out (NWPS DIRPW, or the WW3 partition direction), which for a wrap-around spot may already be partly refracted toward the shore normal. The two frames can therefore differ systematically: most at spots sitting inside a bay behind a headland — lovers-point and monterey-beach, both inside Monterey Bay behind Point Pinos — and least at spots facing open ocean with no headland to bend around — hapuna-beach and suicide-s on the Kohala coast. If a later measurement shows the nearshore frame runs consistently offset from these deep-water bearings, revise the values here rather than changing the gain kernel.

ARCS ARE PRUNED, NEVER AUTHORED. Only optimal_swell_dir is hand-written. The arcs are pruned against it by enrich.prune_arcs_to_optimal, which DROPS any arc whose nearest true sector edge (padded, the boundary in_any_arc uses) is more than ARC_PRUNE_MAX_OFFSET_DEG = 90 degrees from the corrected optimal. Strictly greater-than, so an arc at exactly 90.0 is KEPT. It is a subset operation: no arc is widened, re-centred or invented, and an empty result is left empty rather than backfilled by the orientation-derived fallback. Each entry's arcs_pruned field records what the rule did, computed rather than asserted, so a reader can check the rule was applied instead of values being invented.

TWO THINGS PRUNING DOES NOT DO, both measured on these ten spots rather than assumed. (1) It cannot raise the gain at the corrected optimal: removing arcs never brings a bearing inside a window, so the four spots whose optimal already falls outside every arc — hapuna-beach, thousand-peaks-maui, crash-boat-beach, monterey-beach — stay on the 0.40 rung, before and after, identically. Lifting those needs hand-authored arcs, which this file refuses to write. (2) It is not monotonically protective. A bearing that sat INSIDE a dropped arc scored the in-window floor of 0.25; with that arc gone it is graded by the soft-outside ladder against the KEPT arcs, which returns 0.40 within 45 degrees of a kept edge. On spoils, crash-boat-beach, gas-chambers-aguadilla and table-tops-aguadilla at least one wrong-direction bearing therefore scores HIGHER after pruning. The rule was applied as specified; this is what it does.

IT DOES NOT SAVE HONOLUA FROM THE EAST SWELL. honolua-bay's [77-91] arc — the one that lets an 80-degree swell out of the east rate at all — sits 85.0 degrees from the corrected optimal of 350 and is therefore KEPT under a 90-degree limit. An 80-degree swell scores 0.999 in production today, 0.500 once the optimal moves to 350, and 0.500 after pruning: the whole improvement comes from the optimal, none of it from the pruning. Any limit below 85.0 would drop that arc; 90 was the value chosen, and it does not.

honolua-bay.name: Honolua Bay
honolua-bay.source: Surfline: "NNW to NNE is best to get in, NE is OK"; surf-forecast, surfertoday and surftrips all give NNW-NNE. Researched 2026-08-31.
honolua-bay.notes: Was 84 — east, through the whole of Maui — and scored dir_gain 1.000 on it while a swell from the spot's own facing scored 0.40.
honolua-bay.arc_verdict: At the corrected optimal 350, directional_gain returns 1.00 with the unpruned arcs and 1.00 after pruning — unchanged, as pruning always leaves it: removing arcs cannot bring a bearing inside a window. This spot reaches full gain on its corrected bearing.

arcs_pruned.rule: drop any arc whose nearest padded sector edge is more than 90.0 degrees from optimal_swell_dir; an arc at exactly 90.0 is kept

lovers-point.name: Lovers Point
lovers-point.source: Four sources say northwest: surf-forecast, surfmeteo, boarderspeak, shaman.surf. Researched 2026-08-31.
lovers-point.notes: Was 248, which points at Mole Point 4.3 km away ACROSS the Monterey Peninsula. Roster geometry, from committed coordinates: Carmel Beach bears 190, Mole Point 246, Asilomar 263, Boneyard (= Point Pinos, 36.6393/-121.9314) 314 — so everything from 190 to 263 is peninsula shoreline and the exposed sector starts just north of 314. DO NOT use this spot's baked NWPS node as a cross-check: it is the identical cell to monterey-beach's, (36.62468, -121.895), sitting 1785 m ENE alongshore rather than seaward, so its 96-degree bearing is a grid artifact of NWPS having no wet cell against the Pacific Grove shore.
